overall: Tomorrow, July 2, is forecast to be an exceptionally hot and sunny day in the Washington, DC area, with the NWS calling for a high near 104°F and heat index values as high as 109°F under mostly clear skies and light westerly winds. An Extreme Heat Warning issued by NWS Wakefield VA remains in effect through July 3, signaling dangerously hot conditions well above seasonal norms. There are no tropical or severe convective threats — this is a pure heat event driven by an intense continental ridge.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful spread among source models: ECMWF and HRRR are in reasonable agreement, with expected TMAX values of roughly 101°F and 97.4°F respectively, both assigning double-digit probabilities to the >=100°F bucket. GFS is a notable cold outlier at ~86.1°F with essentially no support for >=100°F, and GEM similarly assigns 0% to that top bucket — these two models inject significant uncertainty into the ensemble. NBM's expected TMAX of ~81.8°F is an anomaly given it simultaneously favors the >=100°F bucket at 18%, suggesting a highly skewed or bimodal internal distribution.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble expected TMAX of 97.5°F and the NWS official forecast of 104°F both strongly favor tomorrow's high landing in or above the >=100°F zone, which is the top even-bucket at 26.3% — by far the single highest bucket probability and roughly 25 percentage points above the next bucket (98–99°F at 1.0%). ECMWF's ~101°F expectation and the active Extreme Heat Warning corroborate the upper-range scenario. Confidence in the >=100°F bucket is moderate-to-high given the dominant NWS and ECMWF signals, though the GFS/GEM cold outliers introduce non-trivial downside tail risk.
